# 23. Hosting & Infrastructure

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Deploy static sites to reliable, portable, free-tier-friendly infrastructure with correct domains, HTTPS, caching, redirects, and access control.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A hosting decision record comparing free or free-tier-friendly static options such as GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify free tier, Vercel hobby, Codeberg Pages, or object storage where appropriate.
- [ ] A domain and DNS ownership record.
- [ ] An HTTPS enforcement rule and certificate renewal ownership.
- [ ] A redirect and canonical host policy for www, apex, HTTP, HTTPS, trailing slash, and old URLs.
- [ ] A cache-control policy for HTML, CSS, JS, images, fonts, documents, sitemap, robots, and manifest.
- [ ] A deploy permissions model using least privilege and MFA.
- [ ] A rollback process for bad deploys.
- [ ] A portability note describing how to move the site to another static host.

## Must Be True
- [ ] The site must be deployable as static files without paid hosting features.
- [ ] The final production domain must match canonical tags, sitemap URLs, Open Graph URLs, analytics settings, and form allowlists.
- [ ] HTTPS must be enforced for every page and asset.
- [ ] The host must support required redirects, headers, 404 behavior, and cache rules or have documented alternatives.
- [ ] DNS records must be minimal, documented, and owned by the client or agreed owner.
- [ ] Deploy credentials must not be shared through chat, source files, or email.
- [ ] Hosting must not inject unwanted branding, scripts, or overlays into premium production pages.
- [ ] Infrastructure choices must preserve source portability.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check DNS propagation, apex and www behavior, HTTPS redirects, certificate validity, and HSTS decision.
- [ ] Check custom 404 behavior and direct refresh on nested URLs.
- [ ] Check headers on HTML and assets after deployment.
- [ ] Check caching does not prevent urgent content or legal corrections.
- [ ] Check deploy preview visibility and robots controls so staging does not get indexed.
- [ ] Check branch protection or equivalent review gates where multiple collaborators deploy.
- [ ] Check bandwidth and build limits on free tiers against expected traffic.
- [ ] Check that provider terms fit the site's commercial use.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid paid-only features for essential functionality unless the client explicitly approves and accepts migration risk.
- [ ] Avoid leaving staging or preview sites indexable.
- [ ] Avoid mixing production and development domains in metadata.
- [ ] Avoid domain ownership under a vendor account the client cannot access.
- [ ] Avoid undocumented DNS changes.
- [ ] Avoid relying on one person's personal account for business-critical hosting.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] Hosting must feel invisible to users: fast, secure, stable, and correctly canonicalized.
- [ ] The client must own or control the domain and deployment path.
- [ ] A rollback must be possible without rebuilding the entire project under pressure.
- [ ] The infrastructure must be portable enough to survive vendor changes.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use generated header and redirect templates where supported by the chosen static host.
- [ ] Use audit reports after deployment to confirm production URLs and public files.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Hosting strategy: static files only, no custom server/database/user accounts/backend admin, custom domain, HTTPS, global delivery, simple deployment, version-controlled updates, rollback, clean URLs, 404, and portability.
- [ ] Free/open-source infrastructure, hosting platform, repository/version control, deployment, domain, DNS, HTTPS/security, CDN/cache, file/assets, clean URLs, redirects, 404/error handling, environments, forms, email, analytics, search infrastructure, performance infrastructure, backup/recovery, monitoring, access/permissions, privacy/compliance, multilingual, blog/content, portfolio/media, static e-commerce, build-free, build-based, documentation, QA, maintenance, red flags, and final approval are checked.
- [ ] DNS changes preserve email MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC and verification records, avoid duplicate conflicts, and point production to production.
- [ ] Live QA verifies homepage, inner pages, CSS, JS, images, fonts, forms, analytics, 404, redirects, HTTPS, metadata, sitemap, and robots.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
